history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — JAIN (Digambara); keep-or-drop decision needed. The most likely referent for the generic 'Jain Mandir, Hisar' is the Shri 1008 Mallinath Digambar Jain Mandir, also called Chota Jain Mandir, at Gandhi Chowk, Hisar (place-listing coordinates corroborated by geocoding). Built through the efforts of the Ramu and Sohanlal families, it was originally a garbhagriha in a large room, later expanded to about 1000 square yards after the committee secured an adjoining house; it was renovated in 2017 under the inspiration of Acharya Shri Virag Sagar Ji. The moolnayak (main) idol of Mallinath Bhagwan is said to be 200–300 years old, with 21 other idols (including Parshvanatha and Shantinath, enshrined during the Panchkalyanak) in a single vedi; the hall outside the garbhagriha is designed as a samavsharan in Makrana marble. Managed by the Shri Digambar Jain Panchayat Committee. Ambiguity: the Bada Jain Mandir at Tilak Bazaar, Hisar, is a nearby alternative referent.

name: Shri 1008 Mallinath Digambar Jain Mandir (Chota Jain Mandir)
town_description: Hisar is a major city in western Haryana, founded as Hisar-e-Firoza by Firoz Shah Tughlaq in 1354. It is known for its agricultural university, steel industry, and historic sites such as the Firoz Shah palace complex and Agroha.

travel.airport: Hisar Airport (nearest); Indira Gandhi International Airport, Delhi (approx. 165 km)
travel.road: In central Hisar, off NH-9; accessible by city road from the railway station and bus stand
